plan.contextChunk: This figure pairs a titration curve for alanine with the structures present at each stage along it. The plot area is tinted pale blue and gridded; the vertical axis is labeled "pH" and runs from 0 to 12 with labeled ticks every 2 units, and the horizontal axis reads "Equivalents of HO-" and runs from 0.0 to 2.0 with ticks every 0.5. A magenta curve climbs from the bottom left in two legs, each a shallow buffering stretch followed by a steep rise, the two joined by a near-vertical jump at one equivalent. Three points on the curve are marked with an x and annotated: "pKa1 = 2.34" at 0.5 equivalent, "Isoelectric point = 6.01" at 1.0 equivalent, and "pKa2 = 9.69" at 1.5 equivalents. Thin arrows run from five positions on the curve out to bracketed structural formulas at the right, drawn with the ammonium nitrogen in magenta and the neutral amine nitrogen in blue: at the foot, the fully protonated cation with an intact carboxylic acid; at pKa1, a bracketed pair of that cation and the zwitterion; at the isoelectric point, the zwitterion alone; at pKa2, a bracketed pair of zwitterion and carboxylate anion; and at the top, the fully deprotonated anion. Aligning each structure with its own stretch of curve shows which species dominates over each pH range and pins down the pH at which the molecule carries no net charge.

interactionPlan.concept: Alanine's titration curve reveals its three protonation states: as hydroxide equivalents increase, the fully protonated cation loses its carboxyl proton at pKa1 to become a neutral zwitterion (dominant at the isoelectric point), then loses its ammonium proton at pKa2 to become the fully deprotonated anion.

interactions.label: Equivalents of HO-
interactions.teaches: Which protonation state of alanine dominates at each point of the titration — the learner feels the curve flatten in the buffering regions (species changing, pH barely moving) and shoot up at the equivalence point where one species hands off to the next

interactions.label: Right panel view
interactions.teaches: Summing the formal charges on each structure shows why the zwitterion at pH 6.01 carries zero net charge — it is the isoelectric form, while the cation is +1 and the anion is -1
Clicking pKa1, the isoelectric point, or pKa2 connects each landmark to its chemistry: 50:50 mixtures of two species at the pKa points versus a single dominant zwitterion at the isoelectric point

demo_steps.title: Fully protonated start
demo_steps.narration: With no base added, alanine is the fully protonated cation: ammonium (NH3+) and an intact carboxylic acid (COOH), net charge +1. The curve starts low, near pH 1.

demo_steps.title: First half-equivalence: pKa1
demo_steps.narration: At 0.5 equivalents the curve flattens at pH 2.34 = pKa1. The carboxyl group is halfway deprotonated, so the cation and the zwitterion coexist in a 50:50 mixture — this is the first buffering region.

demo_steps.title: Isoelectric point
demo_steps.narration: At exactly 1.0 equivalent the curve jumps steeply through pH 6.01, the isoelectric point. The zwitterion alone dominates; switch to Net charge view to see its NH3+ and COO- cancel to zero net charge.

demo_steps.title: Second half-equivalence: pKa2
demo_steps.narration: At 1.5 equivalents the second plateau sits at pH 9.69 = pKa2, where the ammonium group is halfway deprotonated — a 50:50 mixture of zwitterion and fully deprotonated anion.

demo_steps.title: Fully deprotonated end
demo_steps.narration: At 2.0 equivalents only the anion remains: neutral amine (NH2, blue) and carboxylate (COO-), net charge -1. Drag the slider back and forth to watch the species hand off at each landmark.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: Each plateau of the titration curve is a buffering region centered on a pKa where two protonation states coexist 50:50, while the steep midpoint at one equivalent is the isoelectric point — the pH where the zwitterion dominates and the molecule carries zero net charge.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Two-zone layout: gridded pale blue plot on the left (~40% width), bracketed structural formulas stacked at the right, linked by thin black arrows from the five key curve positions (0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0 equivalents). The magenta curve has two S-shaped legs with a near-vertical jump at x = 1.0; mark the three landmarks with small black x's and italic labels 'pKa1 = 2.34', 'Isoelectric point = 6.01', 'pKa2 = 9.69'. Structures share a consistent skeleton — H3N+/H2N on the left, CH above CH3, COOH/COO- on the right with a double-bonded O above — with the ammonium nitrogen always magenta and the neutral amine nitrogen always blue, matching the figure's color code. The slider drives a marker dot that rides the curve with a live pH readout; as the marker crosses each region, the corresponding structure (or 50:50 pair) is highlighted on the right and the others dim. In Net charge view, overlay circular charge badges (+ on NH3, - on COO) plus a net-charge summary (+1, 0, -1) beside each bracket. Clicking a landmark marker snaps the slider to that equivalence value and pulses its structure group.

authoredContext:
Solving the two simultaneous equations gives [HA] = 0.83 and [A–] = 0.17. In other words, at pH = 9.00, 83% of alanine molecules in a 1.00 M solution are neutral (zwitterionic) and 17% are deprotonated. Similar calculations can be done at other pH values and the results plotted to give the titration curve shown in the figure.

Look carefully at the titration curve in the figure. In acid solution, the amino acid is protonated and exists primarily as a cation. In basic solution, the amino acid is deprotonated and exists primarily as an anion. In between the two is an intermediate pH at which the amino acid is exactly balanced between anionic and cationic forms, existing primarily as the neutral, dipolar zwitterion. This pH is called the amino acid’s isoelectric point (pI) and has a value of 6.01 for alanine.

Each leg of the titration curve is calculated separately. The first leg, from pH 1 to 6, corresponds to the dissociation of protonated alanine, H2A+. The second leg, from pH 6 to 11, corresponds to the dissociation of zwitterionic alanine, HA. It’s as if we started with H2A+ at low pH and then titrated with NaOH. When 0.5 equivalent of NaOH is added, the deprotonation of H2A+ is 50% complete; when 1.0 equivalent of NaOH is added, the deprotonation of H2A+ is finished and HA predominates; when 1.5 equivalents of NaOH is added, the deprotonation of HA is 50% complete; and when 2.0 equivalents of NaOH is added, the deprotonation of HA is finished.

A titration curve for alanine, plotted using the Henderson–Hasselbalch equation. Each of the two legs is plotted separately. At pH < 1, alanine is entirely protonated; at pH = 2.34, alanine is a 50: 50 mix of protonated and neutral forms; at pH = 6.01, alanine is entirely neutral; at pH = 9.69, alanine is a 50: 50 mix of neutral and deprotonated forms; at pH > 11.5, alanine is entirely deprotonated.

The figure shows the titration curve for alanine. The x-axis represents equivalents of hydroxide ion and the y-axis represents the pH. It shows isoelectric point and two dissociation constant values.

discrepancies: the five chemical structures are rendered as flat text strings ('H₃N⁺ CH COO⁻', 'CH₃') with only the C=O double bond drawn, rather than the proper condensed structural formulas of the source (H₃N⁺–CH(CH₃)–COO⁻ with vertical CH₃ bond and drawn connectivity)

Add small arrowheads to the leader lines connecting curve landmarks to their structure brackets, as in the source.

plan.concept: Alanine's titration curve reveals its three protonation states: as hydroxide equivalents increase, the fully protonated cation loses its carboxyl proton at pKa1 to become a neutral zwitterion (dominant at the isoelectric point), then loses its ammonium proton at pKa2 to become the fully deprotonated anion.
elements: pale blue tinted, gridded plot area
vertical axis labeled 'pH', range 0-12, labeled ticks every 2 units
horizontal axis labeled 'Equivalents of HO-', range 0.0-2.0, ticks every 0.5

magenta titration curve: shallow rise from origin, first buffering plateau near pH 2.34, near-vertical jump at 1.0 equivalent through pH 6.01, second buffering plateau near pH 9.69, steep rise toward pH 12 at 2.0 equivalents
x-marker on curve at 0.5 equivalents labeled 'pKa1 = 2.34'
x-marker on curve at 1.0 equivalent labeled 'Isoelectric point = 6.01'
x-marker on curve at 1.5 equivalents labeled 'pKa2 = 9.69'
movable marker dot on the curve tracking the slider position with a pH readout
thin connector arrows from five curve positions out to bracketed structures at the right
bracketed structure at 0 equivalents: fully protonated cation H3N+CH(CH3)COOH (ammonium N in magenta)
bracketed pair at pKa1: cation H3N+CH(CH3)COOH plus zwitterion H3N+CH(CH3)COO-
bracketed structure at isoelectric point: zwitterion H3N+CH(CH3)COO- alone
bracketed pair at pKa2: zwitterion H3N+CH(CH3)COO- plus anion H2NCH(CH3)COO- (neutral amine N in blue)
bracketed structure at 2.0 equivalents: fully deprotonated anion H2NCH(CH3)COO- (amine N in blue)
net-charge badges (+1, 0, -1) shown on structures when net-charge view is active

interactions.label: Equivalents of HO-
interactions.teaches: Which protonation state of alanine dominates at each point of the titration — the learner feels the curve flatten in the buffering regions (species changing, pH barely moving) and shoot up at the equivalence point where one species hands off to the next

interactions.label: Right panel view
interactions.teaches: Summing the formal charges on each structure shows why the zwitterion at pH 6.01 carries zero net charge — it is the isoelectric form, while the cation is +1 and the anion is -1
Clicking pKa1, the isoelectric point, or pKa2 connects each landmark to its chemistry: 50:50 mixtures of two species at the pKa points versus a single dominant zwitterion at the isoelectric point

demo_steps.title: Fully protonated start
demo_steps.narration: With no base added, alanine is the fully protonated cation: ammonium (NH3+) and an intact carboxylic acid (COOH), net charge +1. The curve starts low, near pH 1.

demo_steps.title: First half-equivalence: pKa1
demo_steps.narration: At 0.5 equivalents the curve flattens at pH 2.34 = pKa1. The carboxyl group is halfway deprotonated, so the cation and the zwitterion coexist in a 50:50 mixture — this is the first buffering region.

demo_steps.title: Isoelectric point
demo_steps.narration: At exactly 1.0 equivalent the curve jumps steeply through pH 6.01, the isoelectric point. The zwitterion alone dominates; switch to Net charge view to see its NH3+ and COO- cancel to zero net charge.

demo_steps.title: Second half-equivalence: pKa2
demo_steps.narration: At 1.5 equivalents the second plateau sits at pH 9.69 = pKa2, where the ammonium group is halfway deprotonated — a 50:50 mixture of zwitterion and fully deprotonated anion.

demo_steps.title: Fully deprotonated end
demo_steps.narration: At 2.0 equivalents only the anion remains: neutral amine (NH2, blue) and carboxylate (COO-), net charge -1. Drag the slider back and forth to watch the species hand off at each landmark.

plan.keyInsight: Each plateau of the titration curve is a buffering region centered on a pKa where two protonation states coexist 50:50, while the steep midpoint at one equivalent is the isoelectric point — the pH where the zwitterion dominates and the molecule carries zero net charge.
plan.reconstructionNotes: Two-zone layout: gridded pale blue plot on the left (~40% width), bracketed structural formulas stacked at the right, linked by thin black arrows from the five key curve positions (0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0 equivalents). The magenta curve has two S-shaped legs with a near-vertical jump at x = 1.0; mark the three landmarks with small black x's and italic labels 'pKa1 = 2.34', 'Isoelectric point = 6.01', 'pKa2 = 9.69'. Structures share a consistent skeleton — H3N+/H2N on the left, CH above CH3, COOH/COO- on the right with a double-bonded O above — with the ammonium nitrogen always magenta and the neutral amine nitrogen always blue, matching the figure's color code. The slider drives a marker dot that rides the curve with a live pH readout; as the marker crosses each region, the corresponding structure (or 50:50 pair) is highlighted on the right and the others dim. In Net charge view, overlay circular charge badges (+ on NH3, - on COO) plus a net-charge summary (+1, 0, -1) beside each bracket. Clicking a landmark marker snaps the slider to that equivalence value and pulses its structure group.
